name: Czech
modelReview: built 2026-11-13 by Claude Fable 5.2 from usage notes written in Czech with no knowledge of cron, a rule book derived from them, the lexicon and the visible paradigms, after two schedule reads and five blind fluency reads of the rows and seven author passes; the renderer was built by an agent that saw no other renderer and no held-out row: 153 of 153 held-out rows passed on the first judged run. One hard-case row contradicted its rule and was corrected (four years are a list). The forms of the last author pass, about thirty places where the rule book was silent and the builder chose a general rule, and the built output beyond the rows have had no independent read; no blind recovery has been run. After the build one stutter was found and repaired test-first («vždy 1. dne v měsíci vždy 20 minut po…»), and rows were added for the code no row had reached; a sweep of 19,000 patterns in the family that broke Italian (two cadences together in one field) found no wrong schedule. Known limit: minutes or seconds that are two cadences together are listed whole (up to two dozen items), where other languages say the two cadences. The maintainer, a native speaker, ruled that the short style's capitalised table forms («Po až Pá») are normal; 2026-11-13: says when both day fields must match (a day field written from a star beside a restricted one, as in Vixie cron), in rows, rule and renderer written by Claude Sonnet 5.5 from this rule book's seed and reviewed by Claude Fable 5.2; a blind Sonnet reader told these sentences from the union's 16 times of 16, and none has had a blind fluency read
